claims.topic: AVAudioSession.Mode.dualRoute: purpose and exact availability
claims.final_claim: dualRoute (Objective-C: AVAudioSessionModeDualRoute) is a session mode for simultaneous use of the built-in microphone/speaker and one secondary device that supports both input and output. The DocC metadata lists iOS 26.2, iPadOS 26.2 and Mac Catalyst 26.2, each with beta:false, deprecated:false and unavailable:false. It has no macOS, tvOS, visionOS or watchOS entries.
claims.os_sdk: iOS introducedAt 26.2; iPadOS introducedAt 26.2; Mac Catalyst introducedAt 26.2 (beta:false, deprecated:false, unavailable:false). Swift and Objective-C variants have the same platform metadata.

claims.relevance: This is the only Apple API found that names simultaneous built-in and secondary-device use, which fits the candidate of a near-mouth headset plus built-in classroom pickup. claims.topic: dualRoute primary/secondary routes and input+output requirement
claims.final_claim: With dualRoute, the primary route is always the built-in microphone/speaker. The page lists the supported secondary route types as headsetMic, headphones, bluetoothLE and bluetoothHFP, and says only audio routes that support input and output are available. (headphones and bluetoothLE are output port types on their own pages; see F1-M21.)
claims.evidence_excerpt: "The primary audio route is always the built-in microphone/speaker." / "The supported secondary route types are headsetMic, headphones, bluetoothLE, and bluetoothHFP." / "Only audio routes that support input and output are available for use."
claims.relevance: An input-only lavalier or USB microphone is not covered by this list, and a headset must provide both a microphone and output. "Primary" here means the built-in hardware. It does not decide which input the app treats as the learner's primary input. This matches the lead's normalized requirement text.

claims.topic: usbAudio and wired connection on the target iPad
claims.final_claim: usbAudio is not among dualRoute's listed secondary types, even though the usbAudio page describes it as an I/O connection. Apple's iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) tech specs list a Thunderbolt / USB 4 port and never mention a headphone jack or 3.5 mm connector; this is silence, not a documented absence. The model-specific Apple Support page (support.apple.com/en-us/125407) and the combined www.apple.com/ipad-pro/specs product page both say this. So a wired USB-C headset that reports as usbAudio is probably not a supported dualRoute secondary. headsetMic is described as an input from a wired headset's microphone and headphones as an output to wired headphones.

claims.topic: AVAudioSession.Category.multiRoute: input/output and route-change duty
claims.final_claim: multiRoute (iOS/iPadOS 6.0+) is described as "The category for routing distinct streams of audio data to different output devices at the same time", and its page says it "can be used for input, output, or both", so the category supports audio input. That is a capability statement only: actual recording still needs the user's record permission (F1-M24) and the project's source authorization. The page's Important aside says route changes can invalidate part or all of a multi-route configuration and that it is essential to observe routeChangeNotification and update the configuration. The system posts routeChangeNotification on a secondary thread.

verifier_added.evidence_excerpt: 102657: "Background Security Improvements deliver lightweight security releases for components such as the Safari browser, WebKit framework stack, and other system libraries that benefit from smaller, ongoing security patches between software updates." / "Background Security Improvements are supported and enabled for future releases starting with iOS 26.1, iPadOS 26.1, and macOS 26.1." 126604: "Background Security Improvements deliver important security improvements between software updates and are available only for the latest versions of iOS, iPadOS, and macOS." / "iOS 26.3.1 (a), iPadOS 26.3.1 (a), macOS 26.3.1 (a), macOS 26.3.2 (a)" / "Released March 17, 2026" / "WebKit". 100100: "This document lists recent releases, including software updates and Background Security Improvements that are accompanied by security advisories with relevant CVE-ID details."
verifier_added.relevance: This corrects the 'only through OS updates' reading in F3-17 and refines F3-18. As test evidence, record the full OS version including any '(a)' suffix and the state of Settings > Privacy & Security > Background Security Improvements, alongside the Safari/WebKit string.

verifier_added.topic: User-selected microphone modes (Voice Isolation / Wide Spectrum) are read-only to apps
verifier_added.claim: The M5 spec pages list 'Voice Isolation and Wide Spectrum microphone modes' under Video Calling. AVFoundation documents these modes as AVCaptureDevice.MicrophoneMode (iOS/iPadOS 15.0+). The preferred mode is the one 'the user selects in Control Center'. Both preferredMicrophoneMode and activeMicrophoneMode are get-only class properties, and the active mode may differ when the app's route does not support the preferred mode. voiceIsolation 'attenuate[s] other signals' and wideSpectrum captures 'all sounds in the room'. The fetched pages do not state which apps or audio-session configurations (for example multiRoute/dualRoute or a broadcast extension's .audioMic) a user's Control Center mode applies to.
verifier_added.os_sdk: iOS/iPadOS 15.0+; applicability to our session configurations undocumented
verifier_added.evidence_excerpt: preferredMicrophoneMode: "The microphone mode that the user selects in Control Center." Declaration: "class var preferredMicrophoneMode: AVCaptureDevice.MicrophoneMode { get }". activeMicrophoneMode: "The value may differ from the value of the preferredMicrophoneMode property if the app’s active audio route doesn’t support the mode." Declaration: "class var activeMicrophoneMode: AVCaptureDevice.MicrophoneMode { get }". voiceIsolation: "A mode that processes microphone audio to isolate the voice and attenuate other signals." wideSpectrum: "A mode that minimizes microphone audio processing to capture all sounds in the room."
verifier_added.relevance: If the user enables Voice Isolation, a distant professor may be attenuated before capture, which is unrecoverable per the requirement. AVTEST-03/05/06 should log activeMicrophoneMode for each run and test with Voice Isolation, Wide Spectrum and Standard. Whether the modes engage for our session configuration on the M5 is a device-test question.

open_questions: Exact OS on the user's device: is it iPadOS 26.5 or 26.5.2 (both apply to iPads), and what is the build? No fetched official page shows the 26.5 build number, because Developer Releases and its RSS now start around July 2026. Record Settings > General > About.
Exact iPadOS build preinstalled on iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) at launch (arrived 2025-10-22, between 26.0.1 on 2025-09-29 and 26.1 on 2025-11-03) is not documented.
Does AVAudioSession.availableModes include .dualRoute on iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) running 26.5? This needs a device test (F3-20).

Does a wired headset on the M5's USB-C port, via the Apple USB-C to 3.5 mm adapter or a native USB-C headset, appear as headsetMic/headphones (eligible for dualRoute) or as usbAudio (not listed)? This needs a device test (F3-04).

The Apple Store compatibility list for the USB-C to 3.5 mm Headphone Jack Adapter (MW2Q3AM/A), fetched 2026-09-28, lists iPad Pro 13-inch (M4) but not M5, while Support article 108894 recommends the adapter for USB-C iPads generically. Is this a listing lag or a real incompatibility?

While the host app holds an active playAndRecord (or multiRoute/dualRoute) session capturing the mic, does a system broadcast still deliver .video and .audioApp without interruption? Does .audioMic stop, go silent or conflict? The only evidence is a community report of mic loss (forum 794049, no Apple reply). This needs a device test on 26.5 (F3-14).

On 26.5, does broadcast .audioApp contain Safari or Canvas Student playback audio? This is D4-09 and remains open. How does the ReplayKit framework's 'incompatible with AVPlayer content' (D5-M09) affect it?
Does a broadcast upload extension on iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) stay within the reported ~50 MB extension memory limit (D4-12) at the 2752x2064 native resolution?

Do the 'Voice Isolation and Wide Spectrum microphone modes' listed in the M5 tech specs under Video Calling apply to our app's capture? AVCaptureDevice microphone-mode documentation was not fetched in this pass.
Apple sources disagree on the iPadOS 26.7 (23H24) release date: Developer Releases says September 9, 2026, while the security content page and security releases list say September 14, 2026.
What is the exact Safari/WebKit version string on iPadOS 26.5.2? It includes WebKit security fixes, but the Safari Release Notes index has no 26.5.2 entry.
How does a user's per-app input choice in the iPadOS 26 Control Center audio input picker interact with dualRoute's fixed built-in primary route? This is undocumented.

open_measurements: M01 dualRoute gate (F1-18/F1-19/F1-21/F1-31/F1-32). Where: extended DT-G3-05 plus AV03. On the target, record the model, A-number, utsname.machine and the 26.5 build. Log availableModes at three points: before any setCategory, after setCategory(.multiRoute) with nothing connected, and with each candidate secondary connected. Then call setCategory(.multiRoute, mode: .dualRoute, options: [.allowBluetoothHFP]) and setActive(true), and record any thrown error domain/code, the read-back session.category, .mode and .categoryOptions, and currentRoute. Run it three ways: no secondary connected, output-only earphones, and an eligible headset. Classify each outcome as throw, silent default-mode fallback, or built-in-only activation. A successful call is not a pass.

M02 Option acceptance under multiRoute+dualRoute. Record error or acceptance and the read-back options for each set: [.allowBluetoothHFP] (the allowBluetoothHFP page says record/playAndRecord only, F1-15), [.allowBluetoothHFP, .mixWithOthers] (F1-11), and farFieldInput. Before recording farFieldInput, log farFieldCapture.isSupported per port, and leave it off in quality runs (F1-22). duckOthers and interruptSpokenAudioAndMixWithOthers stay out of every run (F1-M02/F1-M23).

M03 Port identity per connector the learner already owns (no purchase). Cases: Bluetooth headset with mic (e.g. AirPods), any LE Audio headset, a USB-C headset, a USB-C-to-3.5 mm adapter with a wired headset, a USB input-only mic, and output-only earphones. For each, log currentRoute.inputs/outputs (portType, portName, UID, channels with channelName, dataSources) before and after dualRoute activation. Record whether it became the secondary, whether it reports usbAudio or headsetMic/headphones (F1-04/F1-05), and whether it reports bluetoothLE or bluetoothHFP (F1-08, F1-M21).

M04 Channel topology under dualRoute (F1-13/F1-14/F1-32). Log inputNumberOfChannels, maximumInputNumberOfChannels, the flattened hardware input order (built-in channels vs the headset channel), how many built-in channels appear (the spec says four-mic array, but that does not mean four app channels), and whether an input-node kAudioOutputUnitProperty_ChannelMap such as [builtIn, headset] is accepted. On output, log maximumOutputNumberOfChannels and whether an output channel map with -1 on the built-in channels confines our AI speech to the headset.

M05 Independent real signals, the core AVTEST-04/05/06 prerequisite. availableInputs is insufficient: Apple says "The active audio session category and mode determine the number of inputs this property returns." Use project reference audio or consenting people. Conditions: quiet hesitant learner near-mouth only; teacher only at the 3/6/10 m engineering distances; bystander only; learner+teacher overlap; three or more speakers with a changing count; changing noise. Per channel, record RMS, peak, clipping, the per-source level difference in dB between channels, and the cross-correlation and lag between channels. Include an explicit duplicated-mono check (correlation near 1 at zero lag, or identical samples). Compare against two baselines: single-route playAndRecord built-in only, and headset only. Fix the thresholds before the runs.

M06 Sample rate and bandwidth under dualRoute with an HFP secondary. Log session.sampleRate, inputNode.inputFormat(forBus:0), IOBufferDuration and the per-port channel formats. Test whether the built-in (classroom) channel is band-limited to the HFP rate: measure spectral energy above 4 and 8 kHz from a distant sweep or pink-noise reference and compare with the single-route built-in baseline. This decides far-teacher quality and is undocumented.

M07 Timing: speech-to-handler latency per channel, inter-channel lag between the headset and built-in channels (clapper/marker), drift over 60 minutes, and the offset between host-app AVAudioTime host time and the broadcast extension's CMSampleBuffer PTS for .audioApp/.audioMic. synchronizationClock is 27.0+ and cannot be used on 26.5.

M08 Input processing under dualRoute. Is setVoiceProcessingEnabled(true) accepted, and does it collapse the input to one channel or change ducking (D4-19/D8-17)? Log isEchoCancelledInputAvailable/Enabled (D8-18; iPad not stated). Record the user's microphone mode (AVCaptureDevice.activeMicrophoneMode: Standard, Voice Isolation or Wide Spectrum; the M5 spec lists Voice Isolation and Wide Spectrum, F1-M01) and whether it changes either channel. Record raw-vs-processed correspondence against the reference.

M09 Course playback coexistence (F1-10/F1-11/F1-17, AVTEST-04). With Safari fixture/Kaltura-style, Canvas Student and Music (control) playing, activate dualRoute with and without mixWithOthers. Record: whether the other app pauses, is interrupted or ducked; where its audio goes (built-in speaker as primary, or the headset over HFP) and its level; whether dualRoute's 'appropriate signal processing for output routes' ducks or cancels it; how much course audio from the loudspeaker leaks into the built-in channel; the effect of hardware volume on both routes (F1-06); and course audio quality in the headset.

M10 Assistant playback under dualRoute (AV02). Play a fixed fixture utterance to the headset only through the output channel map. Measure its level on the headset mic channel (self-pickup), on the built-in channel, and in broadcast .audioApp. No excludesCurrentProcessAudio exists on 26.5, so own-audio presence in .audioApp must be measured, not assumed away. Check that a learner interruption on the headset channel survives and is flagged assistant_playback_overlap.

M11 ReplayKit broadcast coexistence (F1-30, D4-08/D4-09/D4-12). Start the broadcast with the picker microphone on, then off, while dualRoute is active, and also in the reverse order. Log host route-change and interruption notifications, whether session.mode stays dualRoute, which mic .audioMic carries (built-in, headset or a mix), whether .audioApp still carries Safari/Canvas audio with a dualRoute session active, duplicate lag between .audioMic and the session channels, and extension memory at 13-inch M5 frame sizes (the reported ~50 MB limit).

M12 Background and multitasking (F1-29, D4-16). Start dualRoute in the foreground with the audio background mode. Then switch to Safari, Canvas and Notability; use Split View/Stage Manager with the other app focused; lock the screen for 2 minutes. Record per-channel continuity, gaps over 2 s, and the orange indicator. Separately, attempt (re)activation from the background and record cannotStartRecording or the error.

M13 Attach, detach and recovery (F1-09; AVTEST-04/11). Mid-session, turn Bluetooth off, walk out of range, and unplug USB-C. Record the routeChangeNotification reason, the session.mode after the change, whether the built-in channel continues and the length of its gap, whether the channel map must be rebuilt and how long that takes, and whether the learner channel is labelled as a route gap. On reattach, record recovery time. Check that a source the user stopped is not auto-restarted. Also connect a second eligible headset and record which one becomes the secondary.

M14 Interruptions and case closure (F1-26/F1-27, DT-LC-07). Test a banner-style and a full-screen incoming call or FaceTime, and Siri. Close the Magic Keyboard/Smart Folio during dualRoute and record: whether only the built-in channel goes to zero or the whole session is interrupted, whether the headset channel continues, whether overrideMutedMicrophoneInterruption is accepted with multiRoute, the interruption begin/end and shouldResume values, and whether both channels resume.

M15 Per-source stop and indicator agreement (AVTEST-11). Run each stop: headset channel only; built-in channel only (a forwarding gate, compared with a session reconfiguration and its gap on the other channel); the broadcast mic (our forwarding gate; whether the user can switch the broadcast microphone off mid-broadcast is undocumented and is observed); the whole broadcast (user stop from the status bar or Control Center, or finishBroadcastWithError), which ends video, .audioApp and .audioMic together; and the whole session mic. For each, record which OS indicator stays on and which samples reach the receiver after T plus the stated latency.

M16 Unsupported and unavailable paths, kept separate. (a) USB input-only mic under dualRoute: expected not a secondary; confirm the reported behaviour. (b) The same mic as the single M1 input under playAndRecord + mixWithOthers without defaultToSpeaker: inferred only (F2-01/F2-02, F3-M02); the defaultToSpeaker page's USB input-only routing (F1-M22) applies only with that override set, which M1 excludes. Log availableInputs, setPreferredInput acceptance, the current route and whether course audio keeps playing. (c) Output-only earphones. (d) dualRoute missing from availableModes: the UI state is explicit. (e) Below 26.2: verify only as an availability-guard code path; no device downgrade or upgrade.

M17 Separate candidates, never combined with dualRoute. (a) bluetoothHighQualityRecording in default mode on a single route: highQualityRecording.isSupported/isEnabled, input latency for live use, and the EU restriction (F1-24). EU applicability is a user/region input, not a device measurement. (b) A multichannel interface or receiver, only if one is already owned: independently varying channels versus duplicated mono. (c) The optional iPad plus iPhone two-device route (DT-G3-08/DT-G3-10, P3-01): drift, duplicate sound, per-device stop.

M18 On-device recognition on 26.5 (DT-G3-11). Run separate SpeechTranscriber analyzers (D8-19) on the headset channel, the built-in channel, and .audioApp/.audioMic forwarded from the extension over the App Group. First check whether running an analyzer inside the extension fits the reported memory limit. Keep the app backgrounded behind Safari for 15 minutes and record CPU, thermal state, dropped output and model/asset availability. The 27 background Neural Engine restriction (G3-14) does not describe 26.5, where background behaviour is separately undocumented.

M19 Route C compile check. The App Store notes say only that Swift Playground 4.7 "includes Swift 6 and the iOS 26 SDK" and give no minor version. Check whether AVAudioSession.Mode.dualRoute and .farFieldInput (26.2) compile there. If they do not, the foreground dualRoute probe needs route A or H. Route C can never test background, broadcast or extension variants.

M20 Storage audit on 26.5 (AV06). List the app container, the App Group shared container and the broadcast extension's container before and after a session. Verify that only the declared transient buffers, including any IPC ring buffers, exist and that no replayable lecture file remains.
overstated_fixed: F1-13 relevance: "This is the documented mechanism for separate learner (headset) and professor (built-in) channels. Because AirPods input is HFP, the article's example is most consistent with a dualRoute session (inferred)." The article documents channel selection in multiroute sessions. It gives no platform metadata or mode and never mentions dualRoute or allowBluetoothHFP. AirPods input can also use the non-HFP high-quality link (F1-M04). Fix: "documents channel maps in multiroute sessions; says nothing about whether dualRoute exposes both inputs or whether they are acoustically independent (device test F1-32)."

F1-19: topic "silently falls back" and "This describes a behavioral fallback, not a thrown error." The Mode page does not mention errors, and its example is a category/mode mismatch, not a mode missing from availableModes. Adopt the verifiers' correction: errors are undocumented, and the device-unavailability case is F1-21.
F1-09: "so recording is permitted". Fix to "the category supports audio input". Recording still requires record permission and the project's source authorization.

F1-10: "not silenced by the Ring/Silent switch or screen lock". The column carries a "see note" that makes continued playback while locked depend on UIBackgroundModes audio. Add the note and scope it to playback, not continued input.
F1-28: "continuing audio in the background requires the audio value in UIBackgroundModes". Apple says "To continue playing audio". Narrow the claim to playback; background input stays D4-16/F1-29.

F1-04. Relevance: "Bluetooth HFP/LE headsets ... are the only documented-compatible categories". The bluetoothLE page documents an output, system-routed hearing-aid port and no LE microphone input, so drop LE from 'documented-compatible'. Evidence: "Thunderbolt / USB 4 :Bottom" is tag-stripped markup, not displayed text. Quote "Thunderbolt / USB 4 port with support for:" from support.apple.com/en-us/125407, and stop labelling the www.apple.com/ipad-pro/specs product page as apple_support.

F1-03: "The only supported secondary route types are headsetMic, headphones, bluetoothLE and bluetoothHFP". The page says "The supported secondary route types are ..." with no 'only'. headphones and bluetoothLE are output-only port types (F1-M21). Fix: "the listed secondary types are ...; only routes with both input and output are available."

F1-16 relevance: "Under playAndRecord, choosing the headset mic replaces the built-in mic, giving a single input, which is why the dual-pickup candidate depends on dualRoute." The page documents HFP input/output coupling, not replacement of the built-in mic. Label this inferred. Dual pickup can also come from the separate multichannel-interface or two-device candidates.

F1-18: "tells apps to query this property before using a mode". Quote Apple instead: "Query this property to determine if the mode you’d like to use is available on the current device." The word 'before' is project policy.

F1-25 / F1-M04 hash inconsistency: the same WWDC25 251 URL is recorded as 2926c3f4... (F1-25), b04a4bed... (F1-M04 and verifier 1) and db4a8ae7... (verifier 2). The page changes per request. Mark the page hash as non-reproducible and hash the extracted transcript.

F1-11 relevance: "app audio for the AI still has to come from the ReplayKit path". D4-20 is inferred, and whether .audioApp carries Safari/Canvas is undocumented (D4-09). Fix: "on 26.5 the only documented cross-app audio candidate is broadcast .audioApp; whether it carries course audio needs a device test."

F1-14 relevance: "This is a documented way to deliver AI speech only to the learner's headset". The article covers multiroute sessions in general. Its 2-channel AirPods output example conflicts with multiRoute implicitly clearing A2DP (F1-17), so it is illustrative. Fix: "documented for multiroute; under dualRoute and HFP on the target, untested."

F1-22 relevance: "Far-field capture on a Bluetooth device works against near-mouth isolation of a quiet learner". This is an unlabeled inference; label it inferred and leave it to measurement. F1-M02 relevance: "The candidate option set is mixWithOthers without duckOthers" is a proposal whose acceptance with dualRoute is undocumented (F1-11); label it inferred.

F1-27 relevance: "Built-in classroom pickup needs the case open." Platform Security says "iPad models beginning in 2020" and "MFi-compliant case". Applying this to the M5 and to the Magic Keyboard is inferred and should be labelled that way.

Minor metadata fidelity. F1-20 says "returns NO/false" but the page says false. F1-23's os_sdk is Swift-only; the Objective-C variant has no Mac Catalyst entry. F1-16's 'renamed' field exists only in the Swift variant. Record each exactly as the verifiers found it.

review: Post-review corrections from workflow wf_be1a1bd9-37a applied to F1-M22 (defaultToSpeaker condition), F2-31 and F3-15 relevance (unlabelled inference), F1-19 topic, and critic items M15/M16.
